newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE INDEX INCHES UP IN DULL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE INDEX INCHES UP IN DULL TRADE.

text.p: * Lithuanian shares were mixed on Friday and the equities market was not very active, with the central market's volume only reaching 570,000 litas.
* Overall market volume was around five million litas with the secondary T-bill market accounting for the lion's share at almost three million litas.
* The Litin A index inched up by 11.25 points to 2,434.40.
* The official list index also edged up, rising 13.29 points to 955.16.
Lithuanian shares inched up in dull trade on Friday and dealers said they did not anticipate activity to pick up in the short-term.
"Investors seem to be putting their money elsewhere right now, in other markets like Estonia's," said Sigitas Petraitis of brokerage firm Vilfima.
But dealers said that growing foreign interest made the market's long-term prospects look good.
A group of senior fund managers arrived in Vilnius Wednesday for a tw-day fact finding mission and dealers said money would follow.
"We expect a lot more foreign money soon," said one dealer.
The session's gainers included Lithuanian Gas, which advanced for the second straight day after a steep two-session drop, rising to 2.00 litas from 1.96 litas in trade of 52,000 litas.
Dealers said that the state-run gas firm's price fall grabbed investor interest and that buyers jumped at what looked like a bargain price.
Hermis Bank also rose, advancing to 190.00 litas from 180.00 litas in trade of almost 27,000 litas.
Vilniaus Bank was flat at 230.00 litas and none of its shares swapped hands.
